title: Templates and logs
summary: A form is filled in many times; a log collects every record in one list. Save forms as templates, keep logs as Tables with one row per record, and summarise them with COUNTIF, SUMIFS and AVERAGE.
objectives: Keep a log as a Table: one row per record, no blank rows, summaries off to the side.
Make IDs with TEXT, freeze them as values, and work out days between dates with IF for blanks.
Summarise a log with COUNTIF, SUMIFS and AVERAGE.
Save a form as a template (.xltx) and decide between a template and a shared log.

p: Every purchase request becomes one row in the log: same columns, same order, no blank rows, no merged cells, no totals in the middle.
Make it a Table (Ctrl+T): formulas and formatting extend to new rows by themselves.
Summaries go beside or on another sheet, never inside the list.
Freeze the header row so the column names stay visible.
In real life: used to keep requests in a notebook. Now every request is one row, and he answers “where’s my order?” in seconds.

slides.h: IDs and dates that don’t change
p: A request ID must never change. A formula can make the IDs, but sorting or deleting rows would renumber them, so paste them as values once they’re made.
Copy the IDs, then Paste Values (Ctrl+Shift+V), so they stay put.
Dates the same way: Ctrl+; types today’s date as a fixed value.
TODAY() changes every day: right for ageing, wrong for a date something happened.
In real life: sorted the log by value and every request ID changed. Emails quoting PR-004 now pointed at the wrong order.

terms: pasting only the results, not the formulas behind them

p: Three formulas answer the questions people ask about a log: how many are open, how much was approved, and how long decisions take.
Days to decide: `=IF(G2="","",G2-B2)`, blank while a request is open.
AVERAGE skips the blanks, so open requests don’t count as 0 days.
In a Table you can write `=COUNTIF(Requests[Status],"Open")`: it grows with the log.
In real life: reads the three numbers every Monday. When average days to decide passed 5, she added a second approver.

p: A template (.xltx) is a workbook you open as a new, untitled copy. The form, its rules and its protection come along; nobody overwrites the original.
Clear the sample entries first, keeping the headings, formulas and rules.
Save As › Excel Template: Excel saves it in Custom Office Templates.
Open it from File › New › Personal: you get Purchase request1, not the template.
In real life: used to open last week’s request and type over it. Old quantities kept slipping into new orders.

slides.h: What goes in a good template
p: A template is used by people who weren’t there when you built it. Give them everything they need inside the file.
Keep one master template in a shared folder; replace it, don’t copy it around.
Put “v3, May 2026” in a corner cell, so old copies are easy to spot.
In real life: found three versions of the leave form in use. He now keeps one template on the shared drive, with the version in cell A1.

p: Forms that are filled in once per event suit a template. Records that everyone adds to belong in one shared log.
Many teams do both: a template for the form, a log that collects the key fields.
Module 8 collects rows straight into a log with Microsoft Forms.
In real life: keeps the request form as a template and copies five fields from each one into the log. Module 8 will make that automatic.

demo.intro: Finish Rakshak’s purchase request log and save the form as a template.

frames.say: The log is a Table, **Requests**: one row per request, header row frozen.
IDs in **A2**: `="PR-"&TEXT(ROW()-1,"000")`. Then copy and Paste Values, so they never change.
Days to decide, then the summary: 3 open, ₹2,04,700 approved, 3.0 days on average.
The form: File › Save As › **Excel Template (*.xltx)**.

lab.intro: Rakshak’s purchase request log is a Table in **A1:H13**. Add the IDs and days to decide, then the summary in **K2:K4**.

tasks.prompt: In **A2:A13**, make request IDs from the row number: **PR-001** in row 2, **PR-002** in row 3, and so on.
hints: ROW() is the row number; row 2 should give 1.
TEXT(number,"000") pads it to three digits.

mistakes.msg: Pad the number with TEXT(…,"000"), so PR-1 becomes PR-001.

tasks.prompt: In **H2:H13**, the **days to decide**: Decided on − Raised on, or blank if there’s no decision yet.
hints: IF the decided-on date is empty, "".

mistakes.msg: Give a blank ("") for open requests, not 0, so they don’t drag the average down.

tasks.prompt: In **K3**, the total **value** of the **Approved** requests.
hints: SUMIFS(what to add, where to look, what to find).

tasks.prompt: In **K4**, the **average days to decide**, for requests that have a decision.
hints: So the average of column H is enough.

tasks.prompt: Put the steps in order to turn the finished purchase request form into a template.
hints: Save As, then choose the file type.
items: Clear the sample entries, keeping headings, formulas and rules
Choose Excel Template (*.xltx) as the type
Name it Purchase request and save
Open a new copy from File › New › Personal

tasks.prompt: Why keep the log as an Excel Table?
hints: What happens to formulas and formatting?
tasks.explain: A Table grows: type a new request below it and the ID, days-to-decide formula and banding come along. Structured references like Requests[Status] grow with it.
options: New rows pick up the formulas and formatting by themselves, and summaries can use Requests[Status]
Tables can’t be sorted by mistake

quiz.q: The average of 4, 1 and a blank ("") with AVERAGE is…
Which puts today’s date in a cell as a fixed value?
Where does Excel save templates by default?
quiz.explain: Then File › New › Personal finds them.

quiz.q: A form filled in once per visit, and a list everyone adds to. Which is which?
options: The form is a template; the list is a shared log
quiz.explain: One file per event; one list for all records.

points: A **log** is a Table: one row per record, no blanks, summaries off to the side.
IDs with `="PR-"&TEXT(ROW()-1,"000")`, then **Paste Values**; Ctrl+; for fixed dates; blanks with `=IF(G2="","",G2-B2)`.
Summaries: **COUNTIF**, **SUMIFS**, **AVERAGE** (skips blanks). Save forms as **Excel Template (*.xltx)**.
